about: Spread a cart level discount across lines proportionally, so the line amounts still sum to the cart total. The remainder goes to the largest weights first.

cases.name: the remainder goes to the largest weight
cases.about: 100 over weights 333, 333 and 334 gives 33 each and leaves a cent. It lands on the 334 line, and both engines must choose the same one or two registers ringing the same cart disagree by a cent.

cases.name: proportions that divide exactly leave nothing to place
equal weights tie, and the tie breaks toward the earlier line
cases.about: Pinned deliberately. With equal weights the sort has nothing to separate them, so the answer depends on the sort being stable in both languages — exactly the kind of assumption that drifts silently.

cases.name: weights that are all zero fall back to an even split
cases.about: There is no proportion to honour, so the amount is shared as evenly as it can be rather than vanishing.

cases.name: a single weight takes the whole amount
a negative amount allocates proportionally too
cases.about: A cart level discount is negative. It has to sum back to the discount exactly, or the cart total and the line totals disagree.

cases.name: a negative amount places its remainder on the largest weight too
seven equal weights over an odd amount still sum back exactly
cases.about: 9999 over seven gives 1428 each and leaves three cents, which go to the first three lines. The property the whole function exists for, stated as a case so a future change cannot quietly break it.

cases.name: large proportional shares use wider intermediates
cases.about: The final shares fit in bigint, while amount times weight does not fit in a signed 64-bit intermediate.
